observable_outcome: The release machinery is readable through the running control plane: one owner GET route returns the Preview release identity the process was assembled from (release version and the source-derived bundle, contract and docs digests, with the time the snapshot was assembled), the eight promotion conditions of release-contract.md section 4 each with met / unmet / not-observable-here plus a reason, an aggregate promotable flag that is true only when all eight are met, and the rollback target with its recorded rollback history and a bounded retention read. The response names its environment class and the things it cannot observe (Cloud Run running revision, deployed image digest, deploy path, IAP boundary, scale-to-zero). internal/release still imports only the standard library and internal/domain, internal/api imports neither release nor update, no route promotes or rolls anything back, and no digest is written into any document.
acceptance_criteria: A1. Measure the boundary before writing any import, and record each measurement. (i) internal/release is imported by no package outside itself and internal/contracts' test; confirm by grep and report the hit list. (ii) internal/release/source_guard_test.go constrains what internal/release imports, not who imports it: quote the two assertions (TestSourceGuardNonTestFilesImportOnlyStdlibAndDomain, TestSourceGuardNoFileImportsCIOrUpdate) and state that they are unaffected by a consumer-side import. (iii) domain.ReleaseCandidate.CanPromote's exact current signature and every distinct error string it can return (internal/domain/release.go around line 72). (iv) internal/update exposes only Verify, Install and Switch, with no channel-pointer read. If any measurement disagrees with dp-v2-066, stop and escalate instead of adjusting the design.

A2. Import direction. internal/application imports internal/release; internal/api imports neither internal/release nor internal/update. Assert the api boundary with a test in internal/api that parses the package's own non-test files with go/ast and fails if either import path appears, following the verified-matcher idiom of internal/release/source_guard_test.go (a known-positive and a known-negative check on the matcher itself, and a fatal error on a zero-file scan so it cannot pass vacuously). Re-run devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 -run 'TestSourceGuard' -v ./internal/release and record that both guard tests still pass unchanged.

A3. The enumerator lives in internal/release and duplicates no rule. Add a new file to internal/release that turns a candidate plus its assembled source facts into a structured report of the eight release-contract.md section 4 conditions. Per-capability evidence state is decided by calling domain.ReleaseCandidate.CanPromote on a single-capability projection of the candidate (a clone whose Capabilities slice holds exactly that capability), never by re-implementing CanPromote's checks. The new file imports only the standard library and internal/domain.

A4. Two-way agreement with the authority. Assert over an enumerated grid, whose cell count is declared as a named constant and asserted, that the report contains no unmet or not-observable-here condition if and only if CanPromote returns nil, and that whenever CanPromote returns non-nil the report names at least the condition the returned error belongs to. The grid must contain at least one cell of every refusal class CanPromote can produce; enumerate those classes by reading internal/domain/release.go (candidate status, empty capability set, each missing digest field, missing capability target, per-capability evidence, RollbackEvidence, ResumeEvidence). If a class cannot be reached through the enumerator's inputs, stop and escalate rather than inlining a copy of the rule to cover it.

A5. All eight conditions, tri-state, no inflation. Every one of the eight conditions appears in the report with state met, unmet or not-observable-here, a reason, and the named source that decided it. Conditions 1 and 5 are not-observable-here with an explicit reason (condition 1 is enforced by make check in CI and is not readable from a running process; condition 5 needs an incident and secret-scan ledger no in-process source provides). Assert that the aggregate promotable flag is true only when all eight are met, and in particular that it is false whenever any condition is not-observable-here. Do not drop a condition because it cannot be measured and do not restate the eight conditions in the API layer.

A6. Conditions 6 and 7 are decided by the existing docs verifiers, not by new prose checks: use the functions already in internal/release/docs.go (VerifyPreviewReleaseMarker, VerifyRequiredSections over RequiredPreviewSections, VerifyLinksResolve, VerifyCapabilityAnchorBijection, VerifyNoStableToPreviewLinks) and record which function decided which condition. Condition 8 is decided by the seven bundle roles plus VerifySource, VerifyCandidateDigests and VerifyCandidateAgainstContract. Do not add a second implementation of any of these.

A7. The application read model. Add a port and a read model to internal/application (a new file plus the port declaration in ports.go and the view type alongside the other read models), exposed as a Service method gated by callerActor(ctx, RoleOwner) exactly as the other owner reads are. The observer is constructed once from an explicitly configured release source root and caches the assembled snapshot with the time it was assembled; the read does not walk the source tree per request. When no observer is configured, the read returns a distinguishable not-configured error that the route maps to 503 with an explicit code, and reports no version at all. internal/application/service.go and outbox.go are not edited.

A8. Rollback target and bounded retention. The read model reports Route.PreviousStableDigest as the rollback target, the recorded RollbackHistory entries (repository, from, to, reason, at), and whether any Requirement's StableSnapshot still references the target -- computed from canonical state through the existing bounded Requirement page, reported with the number of Requirements actually examined and a flag stating the scan was bounded. Assert that after one rollback the target is empty and rollback-available is false (Router.Rollback is monotonic and clears the forward pointer), and that a second consecutive rollback is refused.

A9. Provenance and the D1 exclusion, in the payload. The response carries the environment class and an explicit not-observed list naming at least: the Cloud Run running revision, the deployed image digest, the deploy path, the IAP authentication boundary and scale-to-zero. Assert the list is present and non-empty in the serialised response. The response must also state that the route it reports is this process's own recorded route, and a process with no route recorded must answer 'no route recorded' rather than an inferred or defaulted route. Nothing in the response, the read model, or the documentation asserts anything about a Cloud Run revision or a deployed image.

A10. HTTP, read-only. Add exactly one owner GET route (GET /v1/release/state) to internal/api/api.go following the existing owner GET idiom (authenticate, require application.RoleOwner, put the caller in the context, delegate to the Service), and declare it plus its response schema in contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml with additionalProperties false and explicit required lists, including the 503 error response. Add no POST route: no promotion, no rollback, no SetPreview. Assert 401 unauthenticated, 403 for a non-owner role, 405 for POST to the new path, and 503 when no observer is configured, in internal/api/api_test.go.

A11. The real tree answers honestly. Assert against the repository root that the report is not promotable and that condition 2 is unmet for exactly the number of baseline capabilities the compiled contract declares, with that number derived from release.CompileContract's output rather than hardcoded; report the measured number. Do not special-case, suppress or prettify this negative result: it is the correct answer and TestRealTreeFoundationCandidateIsNotPromotable already measures the same fact.

A12. Owner console, additive only. Render the release surface in the existing 'Release evidence' section of internal/web/owner.html (currently a placeholder paragraph with no data) plus additive code in internal/web/owner.js: the release version, the unmet and not-observable conditions with their reasons, the rollback target, and the not-observed list. internal/web is edited by V2-065 in parallel: your edit must be strictly additive, must not rewrite or remove the sibling task's section, and if a merge conflict appears in these two files you stop and escalate rather than reverting the sibling's work.

A13. Documentation, without a fixed point. Add prose to the cap-preview-operation and cap-stable-promotion sections of docs/preview/capabilities.md describing what the owner can now read and what the surface explicitly does not observe. Add no new <a id=...> anchor (the capability anchor bijection asserted by TestCapabilityAnchorBijectionBothDirections and by TestFoundationReleaseContractBaseline must be preserved), and write no digest value into any document. docs/preview/index.md and docs/stable/index.md and their release markers are not touched.

A14. Escalate the component edge; do not create it. Record in the evidence the exact ci/components.json change this work needs (application gains a dependency on release) and the consequence of its absence (a change confined to internal/release will not select the application or api component in selective CI). Record the measured precedent that unrecorded internal edges already exist today (application -> quota, api -> quota, api -> runner, cmd/control-plane -> reconciler, runner and store/firestore) and that no test reconciles the declared dependency lists with the Go import graph. Do not edit ci/components.json; escalate it to the tech_lead.

A15. Do not overclaim. State explicitly in the evidence which parts of cap-preview-operation and cap-stable-promotion this surface does and does not make observable, and name the two residual gaps: the automatic Preview-failure response (new claims stop and routing returns to Stable) and the automatic promotion execution. Do not write 'capability exercised' or 'preview journey passed' anywhere, and do not change any capability's status in contracts/release-contract/**.

A16. Existing tests keep their names and their assertions. Report the before and after top-level test counts for internal/release, internal/application, internal/api and internal/domain. contracts/release-contract/foundation-capabilities.json is not edited: confirm by measurement that cap-preview-operation and cap-stable-promotion declare owner_surfaces /owner/, which the owner console change already serves, so no declaration change is needed. Never weaken a declaration to fit the implementation.

A17. Component checks. devbox run --pure -- make component-release, component-application, component-api, component-web, component-contracts and component-docs are each green, and devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/contracts is green. A skipped test is never counted as a pass (gate rule G7); record every skip with status "skipped" and its reason, and never report a skipped suite as a passing one.

A18. Evidence. Create one artifact per touched component: .agents/v2/evidence/V2-066-{release,application,api,web,contracts,docs}.json with ids ev-v2-066-{component}, all with task_id V2-066 and correlation_id v2-066-release-surface. Each records, for every check, the argv actually executed, the working directory, the timeout and a summary stating the measured result, plus the execution environment identifier (uname -srm, go version, devbox environment). Register them with exactly one appended entry each in .agents/v2/evidence/index.json whose evidence_hash is the sha256 of that artifact's final committed bytes; touch no other task's entry. Completion of this task means the ledger test is green with the entries in place: devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/contracts.

A19. Evidence keys are read on the final tree. Each record's evidence_key is its own component key read with devbox run --pure -- make evidence-keys on the final tree where make check is green, with every touched file already git-added; a new file not yet in the index is invisible to that key. If a later commit moves a component's tracked content, re-run the verification and record both the old and the new key rather than erasing the first observation.
A20. devbox run --pure -- make check is green, and it is re-run after the evidence commit so the secret scan reads committed history rather than an uncommitted tree. Record both runs.

A21. No file outside allowed_paths changes. ci/components.json, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum, devbox.*, internal/domain/**, internal/update/**, internal/store/** and contracts/release-contract/** are untouched, and the four existing internal/release source files (release.go, bundle.go, pipeline.go, docs.go) are not edited: this task adds one new file to that package. If the work appears to require a new component or a new ci/components.json dependency edge, do not edit the file: stop and escalate with the exact edge you would have needed.
constraints: Work only inside the assigned isolated task worktree; never push.
Never use git reset, git checkout --, git stash or git commit --amend.

Do not touch ci/components.json, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum or devbox.*; the component dependency DAG and the toolchain surface are V2-045's task. If a new component or a new dependency edge is needed, escalate with the exact edge instead of editing the file.
Do not touch .agents/v2/task-state/** or .agents/v2/packets/**; the coordinator records transitions and packets.
Do not edit internal/domain. domain.ReleaseCandidate.CanPromote is the authority and stays exactly as it is; no new release status, transition or permit kind is added.

internal/release must remain a leaf: any file you add to it imports only the standard library and internal/domain, and never internal/ci or internal/update, in test files or otherwise. Do not edit internal/release/source_guard_test.go.
Do not couple internal/release to internal/update. The relation between route rollback and the update channel symlink stays documentary, as docs/operations/release-local.md states.

Do not weaken any capability declaration in contracts/release-contract/foundation-capabilities.json, and do not edit that file or any other file under contracts/release-contract/. Do not change any capability's status.
Do not duplicate the release contract's rules in the API layer, and do not restate the eight promotion conditions anywhere outside internal/release.
Expose no route that promotes, rolls back, or changes a route. This surface is read-only.
Write no digest value into any document under docs/. Digests belong in API responses and in evidence records only.

Determinism is acceptance, not preference: no fixed sleep, no wall-clock timer, no goroutine in any new test. Waiting is expressed only as bounded deadline polling with an injected clock, and a measured duration is logged as an observation, never asserted as a threshold. Every timestamp in a test is injected.

A skipped test is never counted as a pass (gate rule G7). Record every skip explicitly with status "skipped" and its reason, and record the execution environment identifier (uname -srm, go version, devbox environment) in the evidence.
Never write a verification as passed that was not actually executed. If an acceptance item cannot be satisfied, stop and escalate to the tech_lead rather than fabricating or weakening it.

Do not start a real Provider CLI (codex, claude, opencode) and do not touch any Google Cloud resource. Nothing in this task asserts anything about a Cloud Run revision, a deployed image, the IAP boundary, scale-to-zero, or the deploy path: those belong to the initial deploy gate D1.
Every pre-existing test must keep passing under its existing name with its assertions unchanged. Report before and after top-level test counts per touched package.
internal/web/owner.js and internal/web/owner.html are shared with V2-065, which runs in parallel. Edits there must be additive; on conflict, escalate rather than reverting the sibling task's section.
